solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bitter rivalry's beginning is captured by expert writer

indicators.note: the opening letter is held prisoner inside the other two pieces put together

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled
a Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen

indicators.note: only the opening letter of rivalry is wanted

explanation.surface: A bitter feud starts when a skilled author gets caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes R, which 'is captured by' sets in the middle of the other two pieces. 'writer' looks like an author but is a pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sharp, biting remark or taste is described as bitter or acidic.

clue.text: Like court case without one of the stars

parts.note: as means like, in the way that

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the court hearing

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A lawsuit missing one of its celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the stars' is the definition, so 'one' is the Roman numeral, not one of the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: adjective meaning relating to stars or the heavens.

clue.text: Pray outside church? That's a leap

indicators.note: the word for pray goes around the outside of the church abbreviation

parts.note: to entreat is to beg or pray

explanation.surface: Praying outside a church as a leap of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pray' looks like worship but means beg, ENTREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ballet jump in which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly in the air.

clue.text: Fragrant bananas changing hands

indicators.note: the right-hand letter is swapped for a left-hand one

parts.note: bananas and barmy are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Sweet-smelling fruit passing from one person to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps R (right) for L (left) in BARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a balmy breeze is mild and sweet-scented.

clue.text: Fish caught, having gone out with some angling equipment

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters of gone are rearranged

parts.note: a reel is part of an angler's tackle

explanation.surface: An angler catches a fish after heading out with tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GONE as ONGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large sea eel caught around British coasts.

clue.text: It breaks the law? Not quite prudent

indicators.note: the word It splits open the shortened police force, sitting inside it
the last letter of the law-enforcement word is left off

parts.note: the law is a colloquial name for the police

explanation.surface: Breaking the law is not quite a sensible course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' leaves POLIC, which 'breaks' says is split open. 'the law' is slang for the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a politic move is a shrewd, judicious one.

clue.text: Carry on without one university's funds

indicators.note: without means minus, so one letter leaves the verb

parts.note: to pursue a course is to carry on with it
U is the abbreviation for university, standing for just one

explanation.surface: A college keeps going without its money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the money available to someone or an institution, as in the public purse.

clue.text: New leaderless militia is deployed to prepare to attack

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread out in new positions, so the letters are rearranged
the leading letter of militia is removed

explanation.surface: A new militia with no commander is sent into position to ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops M from militia; 'is deployed' rearranges NEW with ILITIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to wait in hiding for the moment to ambush someone.

clue.text: Bank is broken by River Test

indicators.note: the word for bank is split, with the river letter inside

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A riverbank collapses under the River Test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is an English river, but here 'Test' is the definition: a trier can be a test, as well as one who tries.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: something used to try or test, as well as a person who tries.

clue.text: Italian aristocrat's against returning valuable item

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for a valuable item is read upwards

parts.note: an asset is something of value

explanation.surface: An Italian noblewoman objects to giving a treasure back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ASSET into TESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation: the Italian title for a countess.

clue.text: Kill gangster with shot

parts.note: a shot of spirits is a tot, a small measure
Al Capone is crosswords' favourite gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster is ordered to finish someone off with a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but is a drink; 'with' sets AL beside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang usage: to wreck or destroy completely, as in writing off a car.

clue.text: One admitted to playing no Wagner or Grieg?

definitions.note: a noun, one example of a person from Bergen's country; the question mark flags the example

indicators.note: the single letter is let in among the shuffled letters
the letters of no Wagner are played about with, rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A concert programme that avoids Wagner, featuring Grieg instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges NOWAGNER; 'admitted to' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the composer Edvard Grieg came from Bergen in Norway.

clue.text: Spots containing extremely essential yet volatile gas

indicators.note: the skin-spot word holds the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: acne is an outbreak of spots on the skin

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the letters are rearranged
only the outermost letters of essential are taken

explanation.surface: A spotty mixture holds a gas that is essential yet unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' rearranges the five letters into ETYLE, which 'containing' places within the spots; 'extremely' supplies the two outer letters of essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: Bottle opener vexed nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the two words carry the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A nurse is annoyed by a bottle opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' holds the answer across the join of opeNER VExed. 'Bottle opener' looks like a single item, but Bottle is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: having bottle means having courage or daring.

clue.text: Ultimately people with slippery character, involved in real shrewd manoeuvring?

definitions.text: Ultimately people with slippery character, involved in real shrewd manoeuvring?

indicators.note: the slippery creature plus the final letter are wrapped up inside the shuffled letters
manoeuvring means moving around, so real shrewd is rearranged

parts.note: an eel is the proverbially slippery fish

indicators.note: only the last letter of people is used

explanation.surface: Shifty types, ultimately, are the ones who scheme shrewdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' shuffles ten letters; 'involved in' sets the eel and final E ('Ultimately') among them, 'with' meaning 'next to'. The whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes shrewd, sometimes shady operators who make clever bargains.

clue.text: Originally early Italians? That's about right

definitions.text: Originally early Italians? That's about right

indicators.note: only the opening letter of early is used
the Tuscans go about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: Tuscans are Italians from Tuscany

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether these were the first Italians and is told that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' gives E; 'about' puts R inside TUSCANS. The whole clue also defines, the question mark marking the hesitant guess.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the ancient people of Etruria, roughly modern Tuscany, before Rome dominated.

clue.text: Algae and dead tree turned up on river

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
the Tweed is a river on the English-Scottish border

explanation.surface: Seaweed and a fallen tree surface on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns D and FIR into DRIF; 'on' puts it above TWEED, a river on the England-Scotland border.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: seaweed washed up or floating in the sea, a form of algae.

clue.text: Repeat run after organising transport

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters of repeat and run are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Running again once the travel is sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges REPEATRUN. 'transport' looks like a vehicle, but it is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to transport someone is to fill them with rapture or ecstasy.

clue.text: Underwear thief's caught!

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the word for a thief's is sounded

parts.note: a nicker is one who nicks, British slang for steals

explanation.surface: A thief is caught out by the underwear he stole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' signals sound. 'Knickers!' is also a British exclamation, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: women's underpants, in British usage.

clue.text: An Accidental Man's right for the study of life

parts.note: in music a natural sign is one of the accidentals, alongside sharp and flat
a man's things are his
Tories are the right-wing party in British politics

explanation.surface: An Iris Murdoch novel title seems to be recommended to biologists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Accidental Man' is a novel by Iris Murdoch, but here the phrase splits into a musical sign, his, and Tory. The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the branch of science covering plants and animals in their surroundings.

clue.text: Forest takes time to get burning

indicators.note: takes means adds on, so the time letter is attached

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A forest takes time to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire, the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ardent passion is fiery or glowing, from the Latin for burn.

clue.text: What ends with mate or companion getting letter?

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A riddle about what finishes with a friend, or a companion who receives a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' looks like a friend, like companion beside it, but it is the winning move on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a game of chess finishes when one king is checkmated.

clue.text: Cash perhaps supports old person living abroad

indicators.note: in a down entry, supports means placed underneath

parts.note: ex means former, old
Pat Cash is the Australian tennis player who won Wimbledon in 1987

explanation.surface: Money supports an elderly emigrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash' looks like money but is the tennis player Pat Cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: short for expatriate, someone who lives outside their native country.

clue.text: What's primarily required by one apt somehow to pen epistle?

definitions.text: What's primarily required by one apt somehow to pen epistle?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the shuffled letters hold the letter abbreviation
somehow says the letters of one apt are put together in some new way

parts.note: EP is an abbreviation for epistle

indicators.note: only the first letter of required is wanted

explanation.surface: Asks what a capable letter-writer needs first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges into NOT APE, which 'to pen' wraps round the epistle abbreviation; 'primarily' adds R. The whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: writing paper is what anyone writing a letter needs.

clue.text: One entertained by Snoopy is vociferous

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: snoopy means prying, nosy
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone amused by the Peanuts beagle is loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snoopy' looks like the cartoon dog but means prying.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: loud and clamorous.

clue.text: Drink up around ten? That's good

indicators.note: the reversed drink goes around the figure for ten
in a down entry, up means read upwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink
IO looks like 10, ten

explanation.surface: Drinking up at about ten o'clock is approved of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives PUS, which goes 'around' the figure 10 written as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: devout and virtuous, as a good person might be called.

clue.text: English politician has issues regularly creating stress

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: every other letter of issues is taken

explanation.surface: An English MP keeps returning to issues, causing tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ISE from issues. 'stress' looks like tension, but it is the verb meaning to underline.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stress a point is to underline or highlight it.

clue.text: Old safety device is advantageous

parts.note: a fuse protects an electrical circuit by melting under overload

explanation.surface: An outdated safety device still has its benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something useful or helpful is advantageous.

clue.text: Meet female model going back in perhaps

indicators.note: the turned-round letters go inside the word for perhaps

parts.note: say is used to mean perhaps or for example

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: A woman meets a fashion model who might be returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' gives TISF, which 'in' places within the word for perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to meet a requirement or demand is to fulfil it.

clue.text: Decline to remove bouquet?

parts.note: the prefix de- means to take away, as in de-ice
a wine's bouquet is its scent

explanation.surface: Turning down an offer of a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented verb: to take away the bouquet would be to 'de-scent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a downward slope or a fall in fortune.
